beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay, I think that's actually everything now."

options.text: The Fool's leap, the Lovers' choice, the Empress's patience — a full toolkit.
Only the Fool actually matters, the other two are decoration.
Whichever card came up last cancels out the other two.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "If I ever have to make a call like the old-band choice again, which card do I lean on?"

options.text: None alone — a real reading holds several truths side by side.
Always the Fool, it's the most important card.
Whichever card you drew most recently always wins.

elaboration: That's the whole reason to read three cards instead of one — no single card has to carry the entire answer by itself.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Is there a wrong way to read your own cards?"

options.text: Mostly just forcing them to say only what you want to hear.
Yes — you always need someone else to read for you.
No, any interpretation at all is automatically correct.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Huh. Never thought a deck of cards would make this much sense."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: "One last thing — Dave mentioned he's already finished your risers."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Of course he did. I'll believe it when I see it not wobble."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: For what it's worth — nothing in this deck was ever about who you end up with. Just about what you choose, and how you carry it.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Thanks. Truly — for all of it. I think I finally see the whole toolkit now: the Fool's leap, the Lovers' choice, the Empress's patience. None of it needed anyone else to complete it — but I'm glad you were here for it anyway."
